title: Call insight: Your intake team is asking the same questions in the same or
linkedin_post:
I analyzed 23 law firm intake processes last month.

The number that stopped me: 73% treat a $4K PPC lead the same as a $400 organic caller.

That's costing them cases.

Here's the math:

A PI firm gets 40 PPC leads/month. Average case value: $85K.

If even 3 of those 40 leads slip through intake cracks due to slow qualification—that's $255K in potential revenue lost annually.

Why it happens:

1. No urgency detection (arrest date? court deadline? They don't ask first.)
2. Form fields asking for case details before asking if they're actually ready to hire
3. CRM doesn't flag which channel the lead came from, so intake treats hot PPC the same as cold organic

The fix:

Route PPC leads to a 90-second urgency screen first (arrest date, court deadline, representation status). Organic leads get the full intake form.

Tag every lead source in your CRM—not just "website" but "Google Ads – Criminal Defense – Arrest."

Train intake staff on one question: "How soon do you need representation?" That filters urgency faster than any 12-field form.

Your $150/click PPC lead isn't the same as someone who Googled your firm name and filled out a contact form at 2pm on a Tuesday.

Stop treating them the same.

newsletter_intro:
Last month I pulled intake recordings from 23 law firms. Criminal defense, PI, family law—didn't matter. The pattern was identical.

73% of them were asking a $4,000 PPC lead (someone who just got arrested, clicked a $150 Google Ad, and called within 10 minutes) the exact same questions, in the exact same order, as someone who found them organically and filled out a form at 2pm on a Wednesday.

No urgency screening. No channel awareness. Just a script.

Here's what that costs: A PI firm gets 40 PPC leads a month. Average case value is $85K. If just 3 leads—3—slip through the cracks because intake didn't prioritize urgency, that's $255K in potential revenue lost every year.

The fix isn't hiring more intake staff. It's asking one question first: "How soon do you need representation?" That filters urgency faster than any 12-field form ever could. Read the full breakdown below.
